name: Full Body
tagline: Your whole body, one steady progression.

levels.title: Movement Foundations
levels.description: Start building confidence from head to foot: comfortable movement, breathing, balance and the everyday patterns of standing, reaching and bending.
levels.milestones: 10 controlled chair rises using support if needed; 10 comfortable wall presses; 10 easy bridges; 30 seconds of steady supported standing or marching. Both sessions feel manageable.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Stability and Consistency
levels.description: Turn familiar movements into a steady routine. Build a little more leg, arm and trunk strength while improving balance and foot control.
levels.milestones: 2 sets of 10 chair rises, wall presses and bridges; 10 smooth hip hinges; a 15-second supported single-leg stand on each side; no loss of control as the session progresses.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Bodyweight Strength
levels.description: Develop stronger bodyweight patterns and controlled single-leg loading. Let quality and consistency build your confidence.
levels.milestones: 2 sets of 12 controlled squats and supported lunges; 2 sets of 10 counter push-ups; 8 controlled dead bugs per side; two 20-second side-plank holds per side from the knees.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Ready for Resistance
levels.description: Introduce light external resistance and learn to handle it confidently. Complete the beginner phase with dependable squat, hinge, push, pull and trunk control.
levels.milestones: 2 sets of 12 light goblet squats and deadlifts; 10 counter push-ups; 8 controlled step-ups and single-leg bridges each side; 8 comfortable overhead presses with no trunk compensation.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Full Body Strength
levels.description: Build a repeatable strength base with resistance, carrying and controlled single-leg work. Record your weights or band colour so progress is visible.
levels.milestones: 3 sets of 10 light-to-moderate squats and deadlifts; 10 controlled reverse lunges each side; 8 steady supported single-leg hinges; a 30-second carry without leaning or losing grip.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Single Leg Control
levels.description: Develop even strength from side to side while maintaining a strong upper body. Reduce assistance only when your movement is steady.
levels.milestones: 10 stable step-ups and reverse lunges each side; 8 controlled single-leg hinges each side; two 20-second full side-plank holds each side or an equally controlled knee-supported option; 30 seconds of steady loaded carrying.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Strength in Every Direction
levels.description: Add controlled sideways and rotational work to your strength base. Learn to resist unwanted movement while moving confidently in the directions you choose.
levels.milestones: 10 controlled side lunges each side; 8 comfortable floor push-ups or a strong lower-counter version; 10 controlled band rotations each way; three 20-second one-sided carries each side without leaning.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Integrated Strength
levels.description: Bring your strength and control together across the whole body. Complete the intermediate phase with reliable movement under manageable load.
levels.milestones: 3 sets of 10 squats, presses and rows at your chosen load; 8 single-leg deadlifts each side with stable balance; 8 controlled lunges with gentle rotation each side; two 20-second side-plank holds before adding rotation.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Advanced Strength
levels.description: Build greater strength with stable technique and a clear training log. The challenge comes from appropriate resistance and control, never from forcing difficult positions.
levels.milestones: 3 sets of 8 controlled split squats each side; 3 sets of 8 presses and rows; 8 loaded single-leg hinges each side; controlled shoulder taps without trunk sway. Before power work, demonstrate 10 comfortable squats, 10 reverse lunges and 15 supported single-leg heel raises each side without pain, swelling or giving way; complete a landing-readiness check before jumping.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Controlled Power
levels.description: Keep your strength base while learning to produce force smoothly and, when appropriate, a little more quickly. Make every landing quiet and controlled.
levels.milestones: maintain your Level 9 strength and recovery; complete 3 sets of 3 small jumps with a steady landing and no symptoms later or the next morning, OR perform the low-impact chair-rise option confidently. Readiness for sideways hopping requires a separate landing and balance check.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Athletic Control
levels.description: Build confidence with changes of direction while preserving the strength you have earned. Keep power work brief, fresh and optional.
levels.milestones: 8 controlled multidirectional lunges each side; 3 sets of 8 split squats and single-leg hinges; optional small sideways hops with a stable two-second landing on either leg, or confident low-impact side steps. Complete both sessions without loss of quality and recover to your usual baseline by the next morning.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

levels.title: Full Body Mastery
levels.description: Celebrate the complete progression and make it sustainable. This is your long-term full-body strength and movement practice, with optional power and room to keep improving for years.
levels.milestones: steady squat, hinge, push, pull, single-leg work and carries at a useful load; comfortable neck and foot control; balanced movement in several directions; optional power with consistent landings; reliable recovery and a routine you can maintain. Keep a training log and review your goals regularly. After a break, illness or flare-up, return to the last comfortable level or reduce sets and load before rebuilding.
levels.routine: Four sessions per week: A Monday (MAIN) and Thursday (LIGHT); B Tuesday (LIGHT) and Friday (MAIN). Complete only that day’s session. MAIN: listed sets and repetitions. LIGHT: one easy set, half the repetitions or hold time, with lighter resistance or an easier version. Keep light effort at 2–3/10; skip jumps, hops and power drills. Leave at least 48 hours between MAIN sessions. Start with the two MAIN sessions if needed; add light days gradually. See MedBridge notes for full details.

name: Shoulders & Arms
tagline: Reach. Carry. Push. Pull. Feel capable.

levels.title: Control & Foundations
levels.description: Build shoulder control for comfortable reaching, pulling and pushing.
levels.routine: Four sessions weekly: A Mon/Thu and B Tue/Fri. Complete only that day's session. Start with one set; rest 45-60 seconds. Use very light resistance. Overhead pressing is optional once ordinary arm raising is comfortable.
levels.includes: Shoulder setting, rows, internal/external rotation, biceps curls and presses.
levels.progress: Move to Level 2 when repetitions are controlled without shrugging or leaning, and several sessions and everyday reaching leave no lasting or next-morning increase in symptoms.

levels.title: Strength & Endurance
levels.description: Build strength and endurance for everyday lifting and carrying.
levels.routine: Four sessions weekly: A Mon/Thu and B Tue/Fri. Complete only that day's session. Start with 2 sets where 3 are shown; rest 60-90 seconds. Use a higher support for easier push-ups. The side plank is optional and should be comfortable through the supporting shoulder.
levels.includes: Rows, band pulldowns, counter push-ups, serratus wall slides, arm work and optional side planks.
levels.progress: Keep building when movement and recovery are steady. Add a few repetitions or a little resistance, one change at a time.

caution: Use a comfortable range, light resistance and secure band anchors. Keep breathing and avoid forcing overhead movement or a deep shoulder stretch. Stop for sharp pain, catching, tingling, numbness or weakness. Contact Pain Solution if symptoms persist or you are worse the next morning. Follow any restrictions after surgery, dislocation, fracture or a recent injury. Build shoulder control for comfortable reaching, pulling and pushing. name: Head & Neck
tagline: A little more ease. A little more confidence.

levels.title: Gentle Control
levels.description: Develop smooth neck movement and relaxed upper-body control.
levels.routine: Gentle movement up to 5 days weekly; exercises marked 3 times weekly on non-consecutive days. Begin with one set, then build towards the dose shown. Relax your jaw and shoulders and split the routine if needed.
levels.includes: Chin tucks, neck rotation, shoulder setting, thoracic extension and gentle isometric work.
levels.progress: Move to Level 2 when head turning and daily activities are comfortable and several sessions cause no lasting or next-morning increase in symptoms.

levels.title: Strength & Endurance
levels.description: Build gentle strength and endurance with light resistance.
levels.routine: Train 3 non-consecutive days weekly. Begin with one set and the lightest practical resistance; rest 45-60 seconds. Learn a secure neck-band setup before using it. Comfortable Level 1 movements can continue on other days.
levels.includes: Resisted neck control, manual-resistance holds, deep neck flexor holds, rows and wall slides.
levels.progress: Add repetitions or a little hold time before resistance. Keep breathing relaxed. Return to easier Level 1 movement if symptoms increase.

caution: Move slowly and never force the neck or hold your breath. Stop for sharp pain, spreading arm symptoms, tingling, numbness, headache or dizziness. Contact Pain Solution if symptoms persist or you are worse the next morning. Follow any restrictions after neck surgery or a recent injury. Sudden severe headache, double vision, difficulty speaking or swallowing, new weakness or loss of balance needs urgent medical assessment.

name: Hips & Glutes
tagline: Strong foundations. More freedom to move.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.description: Find comfortable hip movement and a steady pelvis.
levels.routine: Gentle practice as marked up to 5 days weekly; strength work 3 non-consecutive days. Start one set. Choose lying straight leg raises OR standing marches. Bear plank is optional after comfortable rocking. Rest 30-60 seconds.
levels.includes: Glute sets, bridges, clamshells, hip hinges and supported marching.
levels.progress: Move on after comfortable bridges, hinging, getting up and walking, with no lasting or next-morning symptom increase.

levels.title: Strength & Squat Control
levels.description: Build stronger hips and controlled squats.
levels.routine: Train 3 non-consecutive days weekly; rest 45-60 seconds. Choose ONE hip-flexor option: resisted marching, counter mountain climbers or straight leg raises. Choose ONE squat: supported or wide stance.
levels.includes: Single-leg bridges, hinges, band clamshells, squats and optional bear planks.
levels.progress: Move on with level hips, comfortable stairs and lifting, and several sessions without lasting or next-morning symptom increase.

levels.title: Advanced Strength
levels.description: Build loaded strength and single-leg confidence.
levels.routine: Train 3 non-consecutive days weekly. Start 2 sets; rest 60-90 seconds. Choose goblet OR sumo squats and mountain climbers OR seated leg lifts. Jumps are optional, at most twice weekly, with comfortable, controlled landings.
levels.includes: Dumbbell deadlifts, supported single-leg hinges, squats, band side steps and bridges.
levels.progress: Add repetitions or a little weight only when balance, breathing and next-day recovery stay steady.

caution: Use a comfortable range and avoid forcing a deep squat or hip stretch. Reduce the range, repetitions or effort if needed. Stop for sharp pain, pinching, catching, spreading pain, tingling, numbness or weakness. Contact Pain Solution if symptoms persist or you are worse the next morning. Follow any restrictions after surgery, joint replacement, fracture or a recent injury.

name: Back & Core
tagline: Steady in the middle. Confident in motion.

levels.title: Movement Foundations
levels.description: Build confidence with breathing and gentle back and pelvic control.
levels.routine: Practise up to 5 days weekly. Start one set and add the second where shown as this becomes comfortable. Split into shorter sessions if useful; rest 30-60 seconds.
levels.includes: Breathing, pelvic tilts, cat-cow, open-book rotations and gentle abdominal bracing.
levels.progress: Move on when everyday bending and turning are comfortable and several sessions cause no lasting or next-morning symptom increase.

levels.title: Strength & Control
levels.description: Strengthen the front, back and sides of your trunk.
levels.routine: Train 3 non-consecutive days weekly. Start one set and build towards the dose shown; rest 45-60 seconds. Choose open-book OR hands-and-knees rotation for your mobility finish.
levels.includes: Dead bugs, bird dogs, knee side planks, curl-ups and resisted trunk rotation.
levels.progress: Move on when sets are controlled without straining and lifting and turning remain comfortable later and the next morning.

levels.title: Advanced Strength
levels.description: Build endurance for more demanding activity.
levels.routine: Train 3 non-consecutive days weekly. Start 2 sets; rest 60-90 seconds. The rotating side plank REPLACES side-plank holds; the hollow hold REPLACES dead bugs. Use these options only when the simpler version is comfortable.
levels.includes: Planks, side planks, dead bugs or hollow holds, curl-ups and loaded trunk work.
levels.progress: Add a few repetitions, a little hold time or light resistance, one change at a time, while breathing and recovery stay steady.

caution: Move slowly and use a comfortable range. Reduce the range, repetitions or effort if needed. Stop for sharp or spreading pain, tingling, numbness or weakness. Contact Pain Solution if symptoms persist or you are worse the next morning. Follow any restrictions after surgery, fracture or a recent injury. Seek urgent medical help for sudden loss of sensation or normal body control, new marked weakness, or rapidly worsening symptoms.

name: Knee, Ankle & Foot
tagline: From the ground up. One good step at a time.

levels.title: Movement & Control
levels.description: Build ankle movement, toe and arch control, and hip support.
levels.routine: Gentle movement up to 5 days weekly; strengthening marked 3 times weekly on non-consecutive days. Begin with one set and keep a sturdy support nearby.
levels.includes: Ankle pumps and circles, toe spreading, arch lifts, clamshells and knee extensions.
levels.progress: Move on when walking and exercises are comfortable, without lasting or next-morning increases in pain or swelling.

levels.title: Strength & Balance
levels.description: Develop strength and confidence on one leg.
levels.routine: Train 3 non-consecutive days weekly; toe and arch practice up to 5 days. Start one set; rest 45-60 seconds. Use light bands, secure anchors and a sturdy counter.
levels.includes: Band ankle work, toe yoga, heel raises, supported lunges and supported single-leg balance.
levels.progress: Move on with controlled ankle motion, steady balance and comfortable stairs, without a later or next-morning increase in pain or swelling.

levels.title: Functional Strength
levels.description: Prepare for stairs, single-leg tasks and changing direction.
levels.routine: Train 3 non-consecutive days weekly; gentle ankle mobility up to 5 days. Start 2 sets; rest 60-90 seconds. Begin with reverse and side lunges. Turning lunges REPLACE reverse lunges; 3-way lunges can REPLACE both.
levels.includes: Single-leg heel raises, ankle mobility, supported hip airplanes and lunge variations.
levels.progress: Add repetitions or light resistance when single-leg control and recovery stay comfortable.

caution: Use a comfortable range and a sturdy support for standing exercises. Reduce the range, repetitions or effort if needed. Stop for sharp pain, new swelling, locking, giving way, spreading pain, tingling or numbness. Contact Pain Solution if symptoms persist or you are worse the next morning. Follow any restrictions after surgery, fracture or a recent injury. New unexplained calf swelling or pain needs urgent medical assessment; chest pain or breathlessness needs emergency help.

name: Disc & Sciatica
tagline: Build confidence with symptoms as your guide.

levels.title: Comfort & Control
levels.description: Start with comfortable movement and gentle trunk control.
levels.routine: Four sessions weekly: A Mon/Thu and B Tue/Fri. Begin with breathing, then only that day's session. Start one set; rest 30-60 seconds. Mobility options are optional and must not spread leg symptoms.
levels.includes: Bridges, supported marches and squats, hip hinges, rows and foot control.
levels.progress: Move on when several sessions, walking and daily tasks leave leg symptoms stable later and the next morning.

levels.title: Strength & Stability
levels.description: Build hip strength and a steadier trunk.
levels.routine: Four sessions weekly: A Mon/Thu and B Tue/Fri. Complete only that day's session. Start one set; rest 45-60 seconds. Warm up with relaxed breathing and a comfortable walk. Optional open-book rotation should not spread leg symptoms.
levels.includes: Bird dogs, single-leg bridges, dead bugs, knee side planks, squats and lunges.
levels.progress: Move on when bending, lifting and exercise stay controlled, with no lasting or next-morning symptom increase.

levels.title: Functional Strength
levels.description: Build capacity for lifting and more demanding daily tasks.
levels.routine: Four sessions weekly: A Mon/Thu and B Tue/Fri. Complete only that day's session. Start 2 sets where 3 are shown, with light weights; rest 60-90 seconds. Resisted rotation is optional and should suit your symptoms and existing clinical advice.
levels.includes: Goblet squats, deadlifts, planks, supported single-leg hinges and lunges.
levels.progress: Add repetitions or a little resistance when daily activity and recovery stay settled. Return to an easier level if symptoms increase.

caution: Follow existing medical or surgical restrictions. Do not force bending, arching, twisting or hamstring stretching. Stop an exercise if pain spreads farther down the leg or if tingling, numbness or weakness appears or increases. Contact your clinician promptly for new or worsening weakness or persistent symptoms; reduce activity and contact Pain Solution if you are worse the next morning. Seek urgent medical help for sudden loss of sensation or normal body control, new marked weakness, or rapidly worsening symptoms. Start with comfortable movement and gentle trunk control.
